gaps: Upload blocks: no real input[type=file] exists — Browse fabricates a file — so wrong-file-type, oversized-file and parse-failure states were never reached and their copy is unknown.

Automatic retrieval failure and empty-result states are not implemented, so the design's handling of the KF-9 precondition failures (missing account mappings, multicurrency off, CLOSED ACCOUNTING PERIOD, lost QBO authorization, missing products/tax codes) could not be evaluated at all — the prototype never shows a sync error of any kind.
Close (✕): the state map records only 'no visible change, no dialog, no navigation', so whether a real discard-confirmation would appear after a filled-in setup is unknown.
Matching rules modal: content is labelled 'Prototype preview of the product popup', so whether the user can tell which rules will govern this run was not verifiable.

findings.element: Import method (Integration card) select, inside the manual upload panel — set to 'Automated (recommended)'
findings.finding: The data-source mode is settable from two controls that disagree: choosing 'Automated (recommended)' inside the manual panel removes every upload block but leaves the page in the manual panel with Run still disabled, so nothing on screen is actionable.
findings.user_impact: The user has picked the recommended option on both cards, has zero upload blocks left to fill and a dead primary button, and the only escape is a toggle labelled 'Use automatic retrieval' which reads as the state they believe they are already in — so they stall with no next step.
findings.suggested_fix: Make the panel toggle and the per-card Import method selects one source of truth — selecting 'Automated' on every card should switch the page back to the automatic-retrieval card (and re-enable Run) rather than leaving an empty manual panel behind.

evidence.action: Opened the manual panel via 'Upload manually', then set the Integration card's Import method to 'Automated (recommended)' from inside that panel.
evidence.observed: Upload blocks = 0, Run reconciliation disabled=true, the automatic-retrieval card stayed hidden (visible=false) and the toggle above still read 'Use automatic retrieval' — two controls setting the same thing, disagreeing about the active mode, with no message naming what is missing.

findings.finding: Whenever the run is blocked, the primary button is simply set disabled with no tooltip, no inline list of what is missing and no marking on the upload blocks that still need a file.
findings.user_impact: The user sees a dead primary action and has to guess which of several panels is incomplete — the exact generic-blocker dead end that KF-9 identifies as the top source of production friction.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the silent disabled state with a persistent blocker line next to the button that names the specific missing precondition (e.g. 'Add the General ledger export file to continue'), and mark the incomplete upload blocks themselves.

evidence.action: Clicked 'Upload manually' (which produced a hybrid: Accounting side still 'Automated', Integration side flipped to 'Assisted'); separately, filled all three upload blocks to enable Run, then clicked 'Remove' on one chip.
evidence.observed: Both times Run went disabled=true with no tooltip, no aria-describedby, no inline list and no visible change to the upload blocks — chips dropped 3→2 and Run re-disabled with nothing on screen naming what was now missing.

findings.element: Custom start / end date inputs ([period] zone)
findings.finding: The custom date range has no validation of any kind — an end date before the start date, and a range entirely in the future, are both accepted and echoed back as a valid-looking hint while Run stays enabled.
findings.user_impact: The user can start a reconciliation over a reversed or empty period, is told 'Reconciliation started' with no warning, and only discovers the run was meaningless after waiting for results that the copy says can take a few hours.
findings.suggested_fix: Validate the range on change — block reversed ranges and flag ranges with no transactions in them with an inline message, and keep Run disabled until the range is valid.

evidence.action: Selected 'Custom', set the end date (2026-08-01) earlier than the start date (2026-08-31); then set a fully future range 2027-01-01..2027-12-31.
evidence.observed: The hint rendered '2026-08-31 – 2026-08-01' and '2027-01-01 – 2027-12-31' as if normal, error elements on page = 0, and 'Run reconciliation' remained disabled=false in both cases.

findings.element: Integration select → 'how we get the data' zone, for 'Great payments for every one (PayPal)' and 'My store (Shopify)'
findings.finding: Choosing a non-Stripe integration silently removes the automatic-retrieval card and deletes the 'Upload manually' toggle from the page, with no statement that automatic retrieval is unavailable for that integration.
findings.user_impact: A user who set up the run expecting the 'Recommended' automatic option watches it vanish along with the control that would explain the choice, and is left in a manual upload flow with a disabled Run button and no reason given.
findings.suggested_fix: When automatic retrieval is not available for the selected integration, keep the card in place in an unavailable state with one line naming the reason (e.g. 'PayPal does not support automatic file retrieval — upload the reports instead') rather than removing it and its toggle.

evidence.action: Changed Integration from 'mzkt.by (Stripe)' to 'Great payments for every one (PayPal)', then to 'My store (Shopify)'.
evidence.observed: Automatic-retrieval card visible=false, the 'Upload manually' toggle disappeared entirely (visible=false), Run disabled=true, and nothing on screen explained why the automatic option was gone.

findings.element: 'Upload manually' / 'Use automatic retrieval' panel toggle ([how we get the data] zone)
findings.finding: Toggling from the manual panel back to automatic retrieval silently discards every file already attached, and toggling forward again returns empty upload blocks with no notice that the previous selections were thrown away.
findings.user_impact: A user who flips to the automatic card to re-read what it does, or who is nudged there by the mode confusion, loses all of their upload work and must redo it — and because the loss is silent they may not notice until Run is disabled again with no explanation.
findings.suggested_fix: Preserve attached files across mode switches, or warn before discarding them ('Switching to automatic retrieval will remove the 3 files you added').

evidence.action: In manual mode, filled every upload block (chips=3, Run enabled), then clicked the toggle to 'Use automatic retrieval' and clicked it a third time to return to 'Upload manually'.
evidence.observed: On the switch back to automatic, the automatic card returned and Run was re-enabled while any files already picked were silently discarded; returning to manual showed empty drop zones again with Run disabled and no message about the discarded files.
